title: Merging and Resolving Conflicts —

header.html: merge with a fast-forward or a merge commit; explain the three-way merge; use --no-ff and --ff-only; read conflict markers and the status of unmerged paths; resolve a conflict and finish with git commit or git merge --continue; abort with git merge --abort; use --ours and --theirs; list unmerged files
Git 2.50.1: every command was run in the lab

toc.title: A conflict and how to read it

html:
1Two kinds of merge

git merge branch brings the commits of another branch into the branch you are on, so you stand on the branch that receives the work. The result is one of two shapes, shown in the figure.

Fast-forward Merge commit
When The current branch has no new commits Both branches have new commits
What Git does Moves the pointer forward Creates a new commit
Parents of the result One Two
History A straight line Shows the side branch

Two options control the choice. --no-ff forces a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible, which keeps the branch visible in history. --ff-only allows only a fast-forward and stops with an error when the branches have diverged.

git merge feature/search
git log --oneline

Updating b21efce..b6831c5
Fast-forward
 search.txt | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)
 create mode 100644 search.txt
b6831c5 Add search
b21efce Add README

When both sides have new commits, Git does a three-way merge. It finds the merge base, the latest commit both branches share (git merge-base), compares each tip with that base and combines the two sets of changes. If they touch different places, Git merges them on its own. Your hashes will differ from the ones in this module.

A merge commit has two parents. The first is the branch you were on and the second is the branch you merged. git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD prints the commit and its parents, so three hashes mean a merge commit. In the next block, main has a new commit that feature/banner lacks, so the branches have diverged.

git merge --ff-only feature/banner
git merge feature/banner
git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD

fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.
Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.
 banner.txt | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)
 create mode 100644 banner.txt
52fda8fff85b58ea139a96cebb02069fc08d7652 1c15306af9ccd142616d3dedc9f2d39372c07f6c 5b36feb28b0f447fff4634f97fa25e8bd329c38e

The refusal changed nothing, and Git also printed hints that name git merge --no-ff and git rebase (module 5).

Tip

. Use git merge --ff-only when you expect a straight line. It fails instead of quietly adding a merge commit.

2A conflict and how to read it

A conflict happens when both branches changed the same lines of a file. Git merges everything it can, stops, and marks the file. Here main changed the shipping line of cart.txt to 7 and feature/shipping changed it to free.

git merge feature/shipping
git status -s
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U

Auto-merging cart.txt
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in cart.txt
Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
UU cart.txt
cart.txt

git status says You have unmerged paths and lists the file as both modified. UU is the short form. The last command lists only the unmerged files, which helps in a big merge. While paths are unmerged, git commit is refused. A merge in progress is recorded in .git/MERGE_HEAD.

Git writes conflict markers into the file. Lines outside the markers merged cleanly.

Marker Meaning
<<<<<<< HEAD Start: the lines below are from the branch you are on
======= Divider between the two versions
>>>>>>> feature/shipping End: the lines above are from the merged branch 
cat cart.txt

item: socks
price: 10
<<<<<<< HEAD
shipping: 7
=======
shipping: free
>>>>>>> feature/shipping
Tip

. Search for <<<<<<< before you commit. git grep finds leftover markers, and git diff --check reports them. A committed marker breaks the file.

3Resolve, continue or abort

To resolve a conflict, edit the file to the content you want and delete the three marker lines. You may keep one side, the other, or write something new that combines both. Then run git add file to mark it resolved. git status now says all conflicts are fixed but you are still merging.

Finish with git commit, which proposes the message "Merge branch 'feature/shipping'", or with git merge --continue. Both create the merge commit.

git add cart.txt
git merge --continue
git log --oneline --graph

[main 9465c3b] Merge branch 'feature/shipping'
*   9465c3b Merge branch 'feature/shipping'
|\
| * 6e07425 Make shipping free
* | b686faf Raise shipping to 7
|/
* e1ae267 Add cart
* 37c2101 Add README

If you are unsure, abort. git merge --abort returns the branch to the state before the merge: a clean tree, no markers, and no .git/MERGE_HEAD.

To take one whole side, use --ours or --theirs, then git add the file.

Command Result
git checkout --ours file The version from the branch you are on
git checkout --theirs file The version from the branch you merge in
git checkout --merge file Recreates the markers if you made a mess

git restore --ours file and --theirs do the same. In a merge, ours is the branch you stand on; in a rebase the meaning flips (module 5).

Two tools are worth knowing. git mergetool opens a visual merge tool that you have configured. git rerere records how you resolved a conflict and reuses it when the same conflict appears again.

Tip

. When a merge goes wrong, run git merge --abort and start again. It is safe before you commit, and it costs nothing.

4Practice Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1main has no new commits since Ada created feature/search and added two commits. She runs git merge feature/search on main. What happens?

  • AGit creates a merge commit with two parents on main
  • BGit moves main forward to the tip of the branch
  • CGit reports a conflict in every file on the branch
  • DGit copies the two commits and gives them new hashes
Show the answer

Answer: B. The branch has not diverged, so Git fast-forwards the main pointer and creates no new commit.

S2Both main and feature/banner have new commits. Bob runs git merge --ff-only feature/banner. What is the result?

  • AGit makes a merge commit because both sides changed
  • BGit rebases feature/banner onto main and merges it
  • CGit stops with a fatal message and changes nothing
  • DGit deletes feature/banner after it merges the work
Show the answer

Answer: C. --ff-only accepts only a fast-forward, so on diverged branches it refuses and leaves everything as it was.

S3During a merge, git status -s prints UU cart.txt. What does it mean?

  • ABoth sides changed the file and the changes clash
  • BThe file is untracked on both branches of the merge
  • CThe file was deleted on both branches of the merge
  • DThe file is already resolved and ready to commit
Show the answer

Answer: A. UU marks an unmerged path where both sides modified the same lines.

S4On main, Cy sees <<<<<<< HEAD, shipping: 7, =======, shipping: free, >>>>>>> feature/shipping. Which line came from main?

  • Ashipping: free, because it sits near the closing marker
  • Bshipping: 7, because it sits under the HEAD marker
  • CBoth lines, because each side keeps its own copy
  • DNeither line, because the markers hide both versions
Show the answer

Answer: B. Lines between the first marker and the divider are from the branch you are on.

S5Ada is merging feature/shipping into main and wants the whole cart.txt from feature/shipping. Which command takes it?

  • Agit checkout --ours cart.txt, then add the file
  • Bgit checkout --merge cart.txt, then add the file
  • Cgit restore --source=main cart.txt, then commit it
  • Dgit checkout --theirs cart.txt, then add the file
Show the answer

Answer: D. In a merge, theirs is the branch being merged in, and the file must be added afterwards to mark it resolved.

S6Bob started a merge and sees conflicts in many files. He wants the repository back as it was before the merge. What should he run?

  • Agit reset --hard origin/main and fetch again
  • Bgit merge --continue after he deletes all the markers
  • Cgit merge --abort, which restores the earlier state
  • Dgit commit -a to save the files as they are now
Show the answer

Answer: C. git merge --abort returns to the state before the merge started.

4.2 Recall questions

R1How many parents does a merge commit have?

Show the answer

Two.

R2Which flag forces a merge commit when a fast-forward is possible?

Show the answer

--no-ff.

R3Which command lists only the unmerged files?

Show the answer

git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U.

R4Which two commands can finish a resolved merge?

Show the answer

git commit or git merge --continue.

R5What do the lines between ======= and >>>>>>> show?

Show the answer

The version from the branch being merged in.

R6What does git rerere do?

Show the answer

It records a conflict resolution and reuses it when the same conflict appears again.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Fast-forward Pointer moves, no new commit, one parent
Merge commit Two parents; --no-ff forces it; git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD shows them
--ff-only Fails with "Not possible to fast-forward" when branches diverged
Three-way merge Merge base plus the two tips; same lines changed means a conflict
Conflict status Unmerged paths, both modified, UU; git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
Markers <<<<<<< HEAD ours, =======, >>>>>>> branch theirs
Resolve Edit, git add, then git commit or git merge --continue
Abort git merge --abort restores the state before the merge
Take a side git checkout --ours or --theirs; git checkout --merge recreates markers
